title: History, B.A. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Entrance to major requires a 2.00 GPA and third-semester classification, not modeled directly. Extended hist_catalog.json with HIST 1/2 (Western Civilization I/II, used for the plan's 'HIST Survey I/II' items) and HIST 302W. 'LA 283', named in the bulletin's own Second Year Fall semester, could not be confirmed to exist anywhere in the LA department's course listing (unlike LA 83, which is real and already cataloged) -- replaced with a generic 'Second-Year Liberal Arts Seminar' slot rather than guessed at. 'World Language Level 1/2/3' and generic Gen Ed/B.A. Knowledge Domain/Elective pools are modeled generically, same convention as other majors this session. Several semesters' bulletin-stated credit totals didn't fully reconcile against their itemized course lists (a recurring minor source-summarization gap this session) -- not force-corrected. RE-VERIFIED against BOTH the live university bulletin AND the department's own real undergraduate handbook (https://history.la.psu.edu/undergraduate/history-major-requirements/) -- found the prior claim that 'HIST 100/200-level' was 'a normal open-elective structure...not a data-ambiguity wall' was WRONG. The bulletin's own footnote requires 'one course from each of the following field categories: Europe, United States, Global, Pre-Modern' (12cr, 100-200 level), and the department's own handbook page publishes the exact course-number lists for each field -- a real, specific distribution requirement, not an open pool. Fixed by assigning each of the plan's 4 existing 'HIST 100/200-level Course' slots (Semesters 3/4/5/6) to one distinct field, each enumerated with only the codes independently confirmed present in this repo's own hist_catalog.json (a handful of the department page's codes -- e.g. HIST 144H/147/261Y in Europe, 116H/130H/153Y/205/261Y in US, 105H/147/171/175H/189/220 in Global, 105H in Pre-Modern -- could not be confirmed to still exist in the catalog and were left out rather than guessed). The separate 'HIST 400-level Course' pool (3 occurrences, 9cr -- the bulletin actually requires 12cr/4 courses total including HIST 302W's own 3cr credit, so this plan's 9cr of pure electives plus the separately-scheduled HIST 302W already correctly totals 12cr) also carries a real handbook-stated constraint -- 'at least one course which must be in Global History' -- left as a generic, unenumerated slot since no published list of which specific 400-level courses count as 'Global History' could be found; documenting this real constraint here rather than guessing which 400-level courses qualify.
